cities.name: Diu
cities.overview: A small island town off the coast of Gujarat's Saurashtra, a Portuguese possession until 1961, with forts, churches and quiet beaches.

cities.name: Daman
cities.overview: A coastal town on the Gujarat–Maharashtra border, split by the Daman Ganga River into Moti Daman and Nani Daman, each with a Portuguese fort.

places.name: Diu Fort
places.shortDescription: A 16th-century Portuguese sea fort guarding the eastern tip of Diu island, with cannons, ramparts and a lighthouse.
places.description: Diu Fort's massive walls rise straight from the sea on three sides, with a moat cut into rock on the landward side. Inside, rusting cannons, chapels and a lighthouse look out over the Arabian Sea and the offshore prison fortress of Panikota. The ramparts are best walked in the late afternoon for the light and breeze. Diu town's whitewashed churches, such as St Paul's, are a short walk away.
places.history: The Portuguese built the fort in 1535 after an alliance with Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, and held Diu until 1961, when it became part of India.

location.address: Fort Road, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 362520

places.name: Naida Caves
places.shortDescription: A labyrinth of rock chambers and sunlit openings just outside Diu's town walls, beloved by photographers.
places.description: The Naida Caves are a network of passages, chambers and steps cut into soft rock near the Zampa Gate of Diu's old walls. Sunlight pours through square openings in the roofs, and tree roots wind down the walls, creating a photographer's playground of light and shadow. There are no guides or facilities, so wear good shoes and visit in daylight. It takes about 30 to 45 minutes to explore.
places.history: The caves are thought to be quarries from which the Portuguese cut stone to build Diu's fort and walls in the 16th century.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; mid-morning to early afternoon for shafts of light.

location.address: Near Zampa Gate, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 362520

places.name: Moti Daman Fort
places.shortDescription: A walled Portuguese fort town in Daman, enclosing the Bom Jesus church and quiet colonial lanes.
places.description: Moti Daman Fort encloses a whole small town on the south bank of the Daman Ganga River, ringed by bastions and a moat. Inside, the Church of Bom Jesus has a richly carved and gilded altar, and the old lanes are lined with colonial buildings now used as government offices. A walk on the ramparts gives views of the river mouth and the smaller fort of Nani Daman across the water. Mornings and late afternoons are pleasant.
places.history: The Portuguese began the fort in 1559 after taking Daman, and ruled the town until 1961. The Bom Jesus church dates from 1603.

places.name: Nagoa Beach
places.shortDescription: A horseshoe beach about 8 km from Diu Town, known for its calm water and hoka palms.
places.description: A sheltered sandy bay with water sports and shacks, backed by unusual branching hoka palms. It's the most popular beach on the island.

location.address: Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

places.name: St. Paul's Church, Diu
places.shortDescription: A white Baroque church from the Portuguese period, the only one still used on the island.
places.description: An ornate white facade and carved woodwork, and it's among the finest Portuguese Baroque churches in India.
places.history: Built by the Portuguese in the 17th century.

location.address: Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

places.name: Gangeshwar Mahadev Temple
places.shortDescription: A seashore Shiva temple at Fudam, 3 km from Diu, where the waves wash over five lingams.
places.description: A cave shrine on the shore, in which five lingams are bathed by the tide. Pilgrims believe the Pandavas set them there.

location.address: Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

places.name: Jampore Beach
places.shortDescription: A long beach south of Daman, popular for its evening walks and casual food stalls.
places.description: A wide stretch of black sand on the Arabian Sea, with stalls and horse rides. Swimming here isn't always safe because of currents.

location.address: Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

places.name: Devka Beach
places.shortDescription: A rocky seaside and promenade in Nani Daman, lined with hotels and an amusement park.
places.description: A small, busy seafront with a promenade, musical fountain and hotels. It's a popular weekend stop from Gujarat and Mumbai.
